e2_reuse: PARTIAL -- E2's baseline B_e is reused verbatim; E2's WINDOW artifact is NOT usable as an exit and is rebuilt. See rebuild_rationale.
e2_rebuild_rationale: 443 of the 903 (49.1%) have its window_end_ts BEFORE the EPG entry tau -- an exit cannot precede its entry
40.75% of the 903 have duration_min == 0, i.e. participation 'ends' at t0 itself
window_end_ts - tau reaches 433,365 s = 5.0 days, so the window is not censored at the event-day extended session end, which the brief states is E2's own rule
the censored column is False on all 15,742 rows, which cannot be right if any censoring was applied
E2's brief, config and code were never committed -- only its artifacts -- so the declared C, the volume basis, and the censoring rule cannot be read from the repository

rule.C_status: DECLARED HERE, NOT CARRIED FROM E2. The brief says 'C carried at E2's declared value'; that value is unrecoverable because E2's brief and code were never committed. 10 is a round choice equal to the trailing-window length. The ladder is reported as sensitivity on the headline numbers.

censoring.horizon: 20:00:00 America/New_York on the event day (session_offset = 0), the extended-session end
censoring.note: censored events are their own class; no mean is taken across censored and uncensored (E2 DE-3).

end.note: this is why Exit B anchors on the first decay AT OR AFTER tau rather than on the t0-anchored end -- an exit cannot precede its entry.

causality.fact_vs_confirmed: participation_*_ns is the minute the crossing happened (the fact, used by the T2 overlay). participation_*_confirmed_ns is the end of minute (mark + C - 1), the earliest instant the C-minute run is knowable. Exit B uses the CONFIRMED instant; timestamping it at the start of the crossing minute would use C minutes of information that had not happened yet.
causality.clamp_note: events whose confirmed decay still lands before tau exit at tau, i.e. a zero-length hold; counted, never negative.
